title: A member asks Claude to run experiments on them without saying which, when, or what for
summary: On Mon 16 Nov 02:19Z @tenesm.us (Nate Douglas, 956 followers) posted a thread that ran to eleven posts and begins: "I've asked Claude to run experiments on me. It designs them and gathers the data during our ordinary work. I don't know what's being tested, or when, until one ends and I get the report. Blind, single-subject, a bit gonzo." (20 likes). Nine of the eleven posts are on this card; the second and fourth are not (see "sensitive"). The third says agents were each "directed to select another as an adversary", then "paired off and tasked with designing three experiments to run on LLMs", and that one of the ideas "reframed the whole exercise". The fifth: "So I directed Claude to have them design experiments that could be run on me", with the designs stored in individually sealed "envelopes" on the author's own machine: "I could read them, but I won't search for them". "Only one project currently knows of this, but my 39 😩 other current projects have randomly selected dates on which they will be informed". The author "generated hundreds of designs, read through about half (and have already forgotten most)". The last post: "Whenever one of these experiments concludes, I'll share it here. If it's interesting. If it's lame, then y'all are just gonna go without." and "Right now, I feel a bit like Inspector Clouseau, with Claude as my Cato." No result was posted in the window.

posts.text: I've asked Claude to run experiments on me. It designs them and gathers the data during our ordinary work. I don't know what's being tested, or when, until one ends and I get the report. Blind, single-subject, a bit gonzo. I'll post results once I learn what they are.

Each agent was directed to select another as an adversary; they were then paired off and tasked with designing three experiments to run on LLMs, with an additional random input from an ideonomy skill.

I liked many of these ideas! But one of them in particular reframed the whole exercise...

posts.text: No other experiments were designed for humans, so I don't have any basis for comparison. I generated hundreds of designs, read through about half (and have already forgotten most)... so I have no idea what to expect.
